summary: 1942 Aircraft Warning Service cabin on Haystack Mountain, Skagit County; abandoned by 1946, and no source describes what remains today.

facts.design: Newly built cabin used as an Aircraft Warning Service station
facts.status_note: The lookout is gone. No source describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

events.note: Aircraft Warning Service station 'Yoke 2-5' activated April 6, 1942 in a newly built cabin on private land; the register also gives 1942 as the build year
Aircraft Warning Service station deactivated October 16, 1943; the state kept the site
Register and firelookout.com say the cabin was abandoned in 1946

evidence.supports: about seven miles southeast of Sedro-Woolley
first structure was an AWS station cabin, newly built on private land
evidence.quote: Aircraft Warning Service Station "Yoke 2-5", a newly constructed 14 x 32 cabin, built on private land, by the AWS.

evidence.supports: AWS was a wartime program run under the U.S. Army
evidence.quote: the Aircraft Warning Service (AWS) program was initiated under the direction of the U.S. Army

evidence.supports: station activated April 6, 1942 and deactivated October 16, 1943
state kept the site after the station closed
evidence.quote: Upon deactivation the site was retained by the State of Washington.

evidence.supports: wartime: AWS posts were set up when the county feared attack
evidence.quote: when the county was in eminent danger of attack from Japanese forces

evidence.supports: rural AWS posts were usually sleeping cabins
evidence.quote: Usually a sleeping cabin was built

evidence.supports: finding people to man the posts was very difficult
evidence.quote: finding persons to man them was very difficult

evidence.supports: observers were required to report planes around the clock
evidence.quote: Observers were required to report all planes seen or heard twenty-four hours a day.
A cabin was built on the site in 1942 but abandoned just four years later in 1946.

evidence.supports: administered by the Department of Natural Resources
evidence.quote: Administered by Department of Natural Resources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The AWS record says the cabin was built on private land; the state kept the site after the station closed in 1943, which fits the register's state administration.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: Forest Lookouts gives AWS deactivation October 16, 1943; the register and firelookout.com give abandonment in 1946. No source explains the gap, so the story states both. The AWS 'Yoke 2-5' cabin is assumed to be the same 1942 cabin the register describes; no source says so outright. Agency: the record's DNR is supported by the register. No access, visit or remains source was found; the 2023 peak-bagging report at stevensong.com describes the mountain by logging roads and a bushwhack and does not mention lookout remains, so it was not used. No new photos found.
